title: PlayStation Korea Recruits K-Pop Royalty for GTA 6 Ad
description: PlayStation Korea launches a dazzling marketing campaign for GTA 6, recruiting K-pop royalty to promote the game under the 'Plays Best on PS5' banner.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## The Art of Localized Gaming Marketing

The wait for Rockstar Games' next masterpiece continues to dominate the gaming industry, and marketing machines are officially shifting into high gear. According to a recent report by Push Square, one of the most commendable aspects of PlayStation's global strategy is its remarkable ability to resonate with localized audiences while maintaining a unified overarching message worldwide.

PlayStation's current marketing push is heavily anchored around GTA 6, prominently featuring the slogan ‘Plays Best on PS5’. However, rather than rolling out a monolithic, one-size-fits-all campaign globally, the company is executing a diverse array of creative promotional strategies tailored specifically to different regional markets around the globe.

## K-Pop Royalty Joins the PS5 Campaign

In a particularly glitzy move, PlayStation Korea has elevated its local promotional efforts by recruiting K-pop royalty to star in a high-profile advertisement for GTA 6. By blending the immense cultural influence of Korean pop music with the unmatched hype surrounding one of entertainment's biggest upcoming launches, Sony has crafted a localized campaign designed to capture the attention of mainstream consumers and hardcore gamers alike.

This culturally targeted approach highlights how modern console marketing relies on more than just trailers; it requires a deep understanding of what drives local entertainment culture.

## Editor's Take

PlayStation's decision to enlist K-pop stars for its GTA 6 advertising campaign is a masterclass in localized marketing. By bridging global gaming hype with regional pop culture icons, Sony ensures that the 'Plays Best on PS5' message doesn't just translate linguistically—it connects culturally, setting a high bar for video game promotions worldwide.
